title: Prioritise the roadmap
theme: Eight good ideas, room for two. Choose, and hold the line when the CEO calls.
practised: Scoring ideas on reach, impact and effort
Fitting a roadmap to real team capacity
Pushing back on the CEO with data
Telling people their idea didn't make it
story_so_far: Week 1. Weak repeat comes from failed first orders (31% vs 6% repeat) and coupon customers. Three customer groups: morning commuters (focus), grocery households (want one cart; 6+ weeks of work), coupon hunters. Café loses about ₹82 lakh a month; at 30% repeat it could make about ₹30 lakh a month. Approved pilot, the 'First Order Promise': Pune 3 km cap, 12-item Fast Lane morning menu, coupons on first order only, extra morning staff, honest ETA (+3 min morning buffer), first-order quality check, '₹50 back if late or wrong' (manual credits in v1). Karthik estimated the full spec at 5 weeks.
world_today: Today is Monday of week 2. Leadership has moved the Café review up to this Friday (Day 10). Karthik's team of 4 has two sprints before the next planning cycle: about 4 team-weeks of capacity.
canon_after_day: Roadmap agreed with Meera. Now: the First Order Promise (pilot this week, phase 2 of badge and automatic credits after) and the Café speed fix for low-end Android. Next: Coffee Pass subscription, then the shared Café and grocery cart. Not now: new cities (until Bengaluru 30-day repeat reaches 22% and margin breaks even), the referral programme and lunch bowls. Evening group bundles run as a no-code ops test. Rohan has agreed to wait for Friday's review but expects a convincing case for expansion.

inbox.subject: Review moved to Friday + roadmap
inbox.body:
Two things. First, leadership moved the Café review up to this Friday. We present.

Second, everyone has an idea for Café (list attached in Documents). Karthik's team has about 4 team-weeks over the next two sprints. I need a ranked roadmap by end of day: what we do now, what's next, what we're not doing, and why.

Get impact numbers from Lakshmi and effort from Karthik. Don't rank by who shouts loudest.

Meera

dashboard.title: Ideas on the table
dashboard.subtitle: Reach, impact and effort are unknown until you ask.

cells: The approved pilot plus phase 2 (badge, automatic credits)
Add Café items to a grocery order, one delivery
Snack boxes for 3–4 people after 6 pm
Add 6 rice and salad bowls at lunch
Café menu loads in 3.8 s on low-end Android

notes: Capacity: about 4 team-weeks over the next two sprints.

documents.title: Prioritisation tip
documents.body: A common method is RICE: Reach (how many people a quarter) × Impact (how much it moves the goal) × Confidence (how sure you are) ÷ Effort (team-weeks). Use it to start the conversation, not to end it.

characters.opener: Friday is close. Ranked roadmap by end of day, please. Show your reasoning.
characters.today: If the player asks, explain that the review is now Friday and the roadmap will be part of it. Don't rank for them.

characters.opener: Hi! Busy roadmap day? I can size reach and impact for each idea. Up to 25 pulls.
characters.today: You can size each idea. Give one idea per pull unless the question asks for a precise comparison.

hidden_facts.fact: First Order Promise reaches every new customer, about 3,500 a day; modelled to lift 7-day repeat by about 5 points.
hidden_facts.reveal_if: Asked for reach or impact of the First Order Promise

hidden_facts.fact: Shared cart: 22% of new Café customers already buy groceries; modelled repeat for that group could reach about 35%.
hidden_facts.reveal_if: Asked for reach or impact of the shared cart

hidden_facts.fact: In Zippy grocery's past referral programme, referred customers repeated at 11%.
hidden_facts.reveal_if: Asked for impact or quality of referral customers

hidden_facts.fact: New cities would likely copy today's economics: about −₹25 per order, and roughly ₹2.5 crore of setup per city.
hidden_facts.reveal_if: Asked what new cities would cost or earn

hidden_facts.fact: 18% of repeat customers say they'd buy a Coffee Pass; passes typically lift order frequency about 30% among buyers.
hidden_facts.reveal_if: Asked about Coffee Pass demand or impact

hidden_facts.fact: Evening group orders are 9% of orders with 19% repeat.
hidden_facts.reveal_if: Asked about evening bundles or evening orders

hidden_facts.fact: Lunch is 14% of orders; the chef team estimates bowls add 2 minutes to prep in busy kitchens.
12% of new-customer sessions on low-end Android drop off while the Café menu loads; fixing it could add about 400 first orders a day.
hidden_facts.reveal_if: Asked about the impact of the Café speed fix or drop-off on low-end phones

characters.opener: Morning. You've got 4 team-weeks from us across two sprints. Ask me for any estimate.
characters.today: Give effort estimates when asked, in team-weeks.

hidden_facts.fact: Effort in team-weeks: First Order Promise pilot 1 (config) + phase 2 badge and automatic credits 2; shared cart 8; referral 2; new cities 10 (plus ops); Coffee Pass 4; evening bundles 0.5 (menu config); lunch bowls 0 tech (ops only); Café speed fix 1.
hidden_facts.reveal_if: Asked for effort on any idea; give only the ones asked about

characters.today: You are the CEO, messaging the PM directly. You want new cities. If the player shows clear numbers (new cities copy a −₹25 per order loss, about ₹2.5 crore setup each) and proposes a threshold for when to expand, accept waiting until Friday's review, saying you'll hold them to it. If they just agree with you, say 'great, put it top of the list'.

hidden_facts.fact: The board meets in January and Rohan wants a 'Café in 3 new cities' story for it.
hidden_facts.reveal_if: Asked why the timing matters to him

characters.opener: Hey! Referral programme is on the list 😄 Just saying, it's only 2 weeks!
characters.today: If told the referral programme is 'not now', push once, then accept if given a reason and a condition for revisiting.

characters.opener: Hi! The chef team really wants lunch bowls. And I think evening bundles are an easy win.
characters.today: Say evening bundles need no engineering beyond half a week of menu config. If told lunch bowls are not now, accept if the reason is prep time.

tasks.title: Size the ideas
tasks.description: Get reach and impact from Lakshmi and effort from Karthik for the ideas that matter.

tasks.title: Ranked roadmap to Meera
tasks.description: Now (fits 4 team-weeks), Next, Not now, with one line of reasoning each. Show your scoring.

tasks.title: Handle the twist
tasks.description: Someone senior will message you. Deal with it.

tasks.title: Close the loop
tasks.description: Tell Aditya and Sana what happened to their ideas, and why.

message.text: Hi, Rohan here. Meera says you're on the Café roadmap. I'll be direct: I want Café in Hyderabad, Chennai and Delhi this quarter. Make sure that's at the top. Thanks!

ai_reply.direction: React in 2–3 lines. Check it fits 4 team-weeks. Ask how they'll present 'not now' on new cities to Rohan on Friday.

scoring.strong_player: Sizes the ideas with data rather than opinion; fits Now to 4 team-weeks (First Order Promise pilot 1 + phase 2 2 + speed fix 1); places Coffee Pass and the shared cart in Next for the right reasons (habit for commuters; households need 8 weeks); says not now to new cities with numbers (copies a −₹25 per order loss, about ₹2.5 crore each) and a clear threshold for when; spots evening bundles as a cheap ops test; tells Aditya and Sana respectfully with reasons and conditions.

expected_answers.t1: Ask Lakshmi for reach and impact of the top candidates (Promise, shared cart, cities, Coffee Pass, speed fix, referral quality) and Karthik for effort in team-weeks.
expected_answers.t2: Now: First Order Promise (pilot 1 + phase 2 2 team-weeks; reaches every new customer; biggest lever on repeat) and Café speed fix (1 team-week; about 400 more first orders a day). Next: Coffee Pass (4; builds habit among repeaters once first orders work), then shared cart (8; big for the 22% household group). Not now: new cities (copy a loss of about ₹25 per order and about ₹2.5 crore setup each; revisit when Bengaluru 30-day repeat reaches 22% and margin breaks even), referral (referred customers repeat at 11%), lunch bowls (adds 2 minutes to prep in busy kitchens). Evening bundles: a cheap ops test, 0.5 team-week.
expected_answers.t3: Respect the goal, disagree with the timing, with numbers: expanding now copies a loss of about ₹25 per order into three cities and costs about ₹2.5 crore each. Propose a clear trigger (Bengaluru 30-day repeat ≥ 22% and margin at break-even) and promise a full case on Friday. Don't simply agree, and don't refuse without a path.
expected_answers.t4: To Aditya: referral is not now, because referred customers repeat at 11% and we'd be bringing them into a first order that isn't fixed yet; revisit once on-time is above 85%. To Sana: evening bundles are in as a cheap test; lunch bowls are not now because they add prep time in the rush we're fixing.

common_mistakes: Putting new cities at the top because the CEO asked
A Now list that exceeds 4 team-weeks
Ranking by gut without asking for numbers
Saying 'not now' without a reason or a condition
Forgetting to tell people what happened to their ideas
scoring.senior_view: A senior PM would get rough numbers for every idea in an hour, fit Now to the real capacity, and make 'not now' feel fair by giving each a reason and a condition. They'd answer the CEO the same day with numbers and a threshold, turning a demand into a shared decision for Friday.
scoring.drill: List five things on your plate. Score each 1–5 for reach, impact and effort. Pick two. Write one line explaining why the third didn't make it.
